thread:
oncall-bot: PagerDuty P1 -> continuous-batching pool us-east-1 reporting sharp queue growth and latency spike. Alert id: https://metrics.redwood/alerts/1999991234
Maya R: seeing p95 jump and p99 to ~4.6s across multiple cb pools. Queue depth ~1200 on cb-us-east-1-primary, throughput down ~35%. This is across many keys, not a single tenant.
Liam C: digging into logs now, early signs of kv-cache eviction bursts coinciding with microbatch collapse. Logs show alternating microbatch sizes and requeues. Example snippet:
```
2026-03-15T17:58:44Z cb: target_batch=16 actual=2 processed=10
2026-03-15T17:58:44Z kv-cache: evict_count=312 miss_rate=0.84
2026-03-15T17:58:45Z router: conn=ws-17 requeue=1 reason=backpressure
2026-03-15T17:58:45Z cb: adaptive_controller: observed_latency=320ms -> reduce_target
```
Liam C: hypothesis: under a sudden concurrency wave, the adaptive controller overreacts to transient latency, collapses batch targets -> cache churn (hot prefixes evicted) -> more misses -> higher latency -> feedback loop.
Devin S: reproduced locally with a 6k concurrent synthetic run. Controller overshoots when >4x baseline concurrency jumps. Immediate mitigations I can push: 1) hard-cap adaptive target to safe range, 2) enable short static batching window for 30s, 3) soft admission control to smooth bursts.
Maya R: I'm taking lead for mitigation. Plan to roll a config patch to cb-us-east-1-primary: SET CB_ADAPTIVE_MAX=12, CB_ADAPTIVE_MIN=3, CB_REACT_WINDOW=250ms ; also enable kv_cache.eviction_throttle=true. Rolling now.
Maya R: issuing commands:
```
infra deploy-config --pool cb-us-east-1-primary --set CB_ADAPTIVE_MAX=12 CB_ADAPTIVE_MIN=3 CB_REACT_WINDOW=250ms
infra deploy-config --pool cb-us-east-1-primary --set kv_cache.eviction_throttle=true
```
oncall-bot: Deploy job started: job/1999991234-cb-config-rollout (initiated by Maya R)
Sahil P: I'll open support tags and notify customer-success. Early telemetry shows two high-volume customers W-4487 and W-9921 experiencing retries/5xx between 17:57-18:05 UTC. Filing tickets: https://support/rr/4487, https://support/rr/9921 :boom:
Liam C: adding router fallback plan if config patch doesn't recover quickly: route 15% to a compact model variant and switch cache to prefix-only to limit state growth. Command we can run quickly:
```
router update --pool cb-us-east-1-primary --fallback model-small --fallback-rate 0.15 --cache-mode prefix-only
```
Devin S: Patch progress: performing rolling update, starting with 4 hosts, monitoring. Also enabling admission control: admission_window_ms=60 to damp bursts.
Maya R: patch applied to first 4/10 hosts. Metrics on patched hosts: p99 down from 4.6s -> ~1.8s, queue depth on those hosts down from 1200 -> ~250. Still watching unpatched hosts.
oncall-bot: Deploy job update: job/1999991234-cb-config-rollout -> 4/10 hosts success
Liam C: note from logs during rollout: requeue rate halved on patched hosts. KV eviction rate down ~70% there.
Maya R: rolling to remaining hosts. ETA ~6 minutes.
Sahil P: support note: informing affected workspaces that we are mitigating, recommended retries should succeed; no indication of data loss. Sending interim update via support channel.
Maya R: deploy finished: all 10/10 hosts patched at 18:11:39 UTC. Observed cluster-wide improvement: p95 ~0.7s, p99 ~1.2s, queue depth normalized <180. KV eviction spikes stopped.
oncall-bot: Deploy job succeeded job/1999991234-cb-config-rollout -> completed
Devin S: holding router fallback as a contingency. After stabilization, I recommend these follow-ups: 1) implement controller safety caps in code (not only config), 2) enforce KV cache soft-cap with graceful eviction and degradation path, 3) add synthetic disruption tests that emulate a sudden 5-10x concurrency wave.
